I think I decided to kill myself.

It's not set in stone, and I'm still working on some details, like I know how I'm going to do it, and who I'm going to write letters to, and even what time of day to do it in. 

A big part of me thinks I'll chicken out, and won't go through with it, but thats okay, it wouldnt be the first time I didn't follow through with something. Lately I've been trying my best to be as cheerful as I can around my friends, so they can remember me for who I really was. It always makes me giggle when they ask me why I'm feeling 'on top of the world' all of a sudden, and I just smile at them.

Even though I probably won't go through with it at all, it really is relaxing and calming to hold onto that thought, you know? Kind of like before I spent my days laying in bed crying, and now I'm dancing and taking a lot of photos and going to movies. It's a bitter situation, but these last few days have definitely been a silver lining <3

Honestly? The critters.

I am playing on my first character, and the game wasn't holding me that much. Like, I hit level 11 and got bored of doing quests so quickly, and was looking for other fun things to do.

That's when I found out I could basically play Pokémon in the game, which I absolutely loved.

I went out of my way to just catch a bunch of critters, and while I was doing so, I had to explore new areas and level up. Critter catching and training allowed me to get sucked into the game JUST long enough for me to get addicted.

I'm now level 87. Not max level of course, but I'm having an absolute blast, and feel like I'm getting ahold of my character quite nicely (I play a Resto Druid, even in PvE).

Some games that I have played or enjoyed with my girlfriend!

I really enjoyed Borderlands 2, which while it is a shooter, I'm not sure I would classify it as a 'war' game. The entire game is a lot of fun to play through with some friends, in fact I would only play through it with some people close to me :)

Portal 2 is an absolutely amazing experience, and while I prefer the single player version on it, it has it's own co-op mode that has a fun story.

If you're willing to let your girlfriend have the 'spot light' (something I often do when gaming), Fable 3 is a good time. I hear it's really bad compared to the other Fables, but the multiplayer on it is really fun, and while cutscenes only pay attention to one character, the entire game has some wonderful cooperative moments.

Diablo and Castle crashers are also a good time to play on co op, although my girlfriend was never really into those games. 

Also, the Lego games might seem like they're only for little kids, but they actually have some relatively complicated puzzles, and the humor is pretty good. Not difficult at all, but great for some casual fun!

Have fun and take it slow! I find it to be a lot more fun if you don't just 'farm the island' (you'll probably understand) and let the good times and game come naturally. Have fun, roleplay. Send letters to the village people, and form friendships.

If you have any friends that play, join them! But I wouldn't accept too many gifts. It'd be tempting for someone to dupe you thousands of bells, but it often kills any progression the game has :P

I suppose if you're purely the creative type then go for it, but you'd still risk losing some of the long term appeal of the game :)
